quote: Never measure the height of a mountain until you have reached the top. Then you will see how low it was.
source: Dag Hammarskjöld, Markings, the entries for 1925 to 1930 (trans. Leif Sjöberg and W. H. Auden, 1964)
note: Corrected: the entry stands in the opening block of Markings, the entries headed 1925 to 1930, and not in 1958. Hammarskjöld was a young man when he wrote it. The English wording is Sjöberg and Auden’s of 1964 and is unchanged.

evidence.where: The English Wikiquote page for Hammarskjöld, whose Markings section is headed as the Sjöberg and Auden translation of 1964 and which prints this line under the year block 1925 to 1930 with the Swedish original Mät aldrig bergets höjd förrän du nått toppen. Då skall du se hur lågt det var. A quotation database citing a Google Books copy of the 1964 Knopf edition places the line on page 3, which is the first page of text and therefore inside that same opening block. Full text search inside the Internet Archive copies was not available, so no printed page was read.
evidence.edition: Markings, trans. Leif Sjöberg and W. H. Auden (Knopf, 1964), from Vägmärken (1963)

reason: The line is genuinely Hammarskjöld’s and the wording and translators are right, but the proposed locator of 1958 has nothing behind it: two independent sources put the entry in the first year block of the book, one by the year heading and one by the page number. Hammarskjöld is new to the year, so there is no cap or repetition problem.
